claim: The first real workload maps into Canon. All 215 entries of the zachshallbetter.com corpus import as valid Canon envelopes, land in a chained journal (226 records: 215 content + 1 derived + 10 relations), freeze, and resolve as surfaces; over that real content a public reader's surface contains no private entry, with a control assertion proving the check can fail. The mapping preserves three distinctions the source keeps and refuses to launder one it collapses: 'unlisted' (2 entries) lands as neither public nor private; the 142 private entries land at owner access and unpublished; model-generated Semantic Article Field material lands as a SEPARATE derived-provenance envelope, never merged into authored content; and the source's dual-vocabulary 'status' field -- publication states and project-lifecycle labels sharing one column, exactly the collapse DESIGN.md 3.5 prohibits, found in the owner's own live data -- produces 22 findings with lifecycle labels preserved verbatim and no publication state inferred from them. 12/12 vectors run against the real corpus manifest, not a fixture authored to pass.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested against a REAL corpus. This does NOT establish empirical usefulness: no human has used the result, nothing is deployed, and no live state was touched. rcp-001 remains an active obligation, not a discharged one.

Reconciliation requires owner-authorized credentials and is deferred to SCMS-029. Nothing here claims the corpus is current.

claim: The round-trip closes. zachshallbetter.com's real reader routes (/writing, /work and their detail pages) resolve as surfaces over the 215-entry migrated corpus: no public route exposes any of the 142 private entries; a private detail route is refused with a closed failure class rather than rendered empty; the owner's view differs from the public view by exactly the private set; unlisted content is reachable by link and absent from index, feed, and sitemap; and both expressions of a public route present no private subject, with control assertions proving each scan can fail. The slice establishes one rule: a feed is an expression of the same ResolvedSurface as its page, never a second query. deriveFeed takes no snapshot and no access level, and hydration runs through an injected lookup called for exactly the surface's members -- asserted by recording every subject the hydrator was asked for and comparing it to the member set. 11/11 vectors.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested for the reader path over a real corpus. Establishes nothing about rendering, deployment, caching under load, or the owner-gated authoring routes (E12).

details.ruleEstablished: A feed is an expression of the page's ResolvedSurface, never a second query. The classic draft-in-RSS leak is a drift between two query paths; removing the second path removes the drift by construction rather than by discipline.
details.findings: Two, both caught by vectors before landing. (1) NR-scms-004: SCMS-028 declared an 'unlisted' attribute 'so discovery lenses can exclude it' and no lens consumed it, so both unlisted entries appeared in the public index -- the declaration-without-a-consumer class, fourth instance, committed by this project. Fixed by inverting to a positive always-present 'listed' flag so discovery excludes on absence. (2) A substring leak scan flagged the two-character slug 'ma' occurring inside markup; the scan was made token-wise rather than relaxed.

claim: The authoring surface exists as a ResolvedSurface, and the write path is authorized for the first time. The editor derives its operations from the live ContractRegistry, so it cannot offer an affordance nothing implements; unimplemented intents are withheld with a legible reason rather than silently absent; a compensatable operation is not offered while its compensation is unregistered; effect class and reversibility are carried from the contract's own declaration so an expression cannot present publishing as saving; the owner's editor resolves a private draft with operations available while a public reader gets every operation withheld and no surface at all on private content. Building the 'offering is not permission' vector exposed NR-scms-005: no handler authorized anything. Corrected by a registration-checked minAuthority on each contract plus a proven authority on the execution context, enforced once in ContractRegistry.execute before dispatch. 9/9 authoring vectors, 3 new gate vectors in contracts, and 147/147 across all fourteen packages.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested. The authoring SURFACE is specified and gated; no editor is rendered, nothing is deployed, and SH-8's visual half remains open.

details.securityFinding: NR-scms-005 -- the governed write path performed no authorization. An anonymous public caller promoted an owner-private draft using a self-declared attestation and a self-declared authority string. Found by refusing to trust a vector that passed: it asserted the refusal of an unauthorized call without asserting the REASON, and the call had in fact been refused for a missing attestation.
details.claimCorrected: The register's promotion claim asserted that promotion 'refuses unauthorised candidates'. It did not. The claim has been corrected in place with the falsification recorded rather than the wording quietly softened.
details.remainsOpen: Attestations are still caller-supplied and unverified: disposition QUALIFIED is trusted because it was passed in. The authority gate means only an owner can exploit this, which lowers severity without closing it -- the evidence gate still accepts evidence from the party being gated. Closing it requires deciding who issues and signs attestations, an owner authority question. Registered as scms-blocker-003 and SH-13.

claim: The transactional outbox exists and 'nothing happens without an emission' is a checked property rather than a slogan. Emission lives inside CanonJournal's landing path, so no code path can land a record without emitting: append, supersede and revoke each emit exactly once; a write rejected by validation emits nothing; an idempotent re-land of identical content emits nothing new. Event ids are gapless and monotonic from zero, the event stream and the hash-linked receipt chain agree change-for-change, and replay from EVERY cursor position -- including the null backfill cursor and every mid-stream reconnect point -- reconstructs the full stream with nothing missing, which is P10's stated 'no event loss' criterion. A cursor ahead of the stream returns silence rather than throwing. Events name a revision and carry minimumAccess so fan-out can decide who may be told without reading content back; a vector confirms no record content appears in an event. The integrity checker is proven able to fail on all four of its finding classes. Over the real 226-record corpus every landed record announced exactly once. 10/10 vectors; 163/163 across fifteen packages.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested for EMISSION only. Establishes nothing about delivery: nothing is transported, no subscriber exists, and no client has reconnected. The in-memory single-operation commit is the right semantics but is not a database transaction -- durability and concurrent commit remain open under SH-1.

details.designDecision: The outbox is inside CanonJournal rather than beside it. An emitter the write path must remember to call is the exact shape that failed in NR-scms-005 and again in NR-scms-006; making emission part of what landing IS removes the opportunity to forget. This does not couple Canon to transport -- the outbox holds rows, not connections, and DESIGN.md 8.1 already frames it as the integrity stream that audit, projections, dead-letter handling and subscribers all consume.

claim: The authoring surface exists and its honesty properties are tested as data rather than drawn as styling. editorView() returns what an author sees: publish carries E3/consequential weight while save carries E1/routine so the interface cannot present them as one gesture, and a compensatable operation names its reversal before it is taken; every disabled operation carries a reason string, asserted for all operations rather than spot-checked; the provenance chip is SCMS-017's implementation reused verbatim rather than reimplemented, and it flips to 'local, unsent' on the first keystroke; the four state axes render as four values and are never collapsed to one status; conflict keeps slots editable while freezing consequential action, which is DESIGN.md 8.6's asymmetry rendered; and operations nothing implements are explained rather than omitted. The 25 findings the migration refused to guess on surface on the entry itself with a count in the index, so the ambiguity the importer declined to launder becomes the owner's decision. 11/11 vectors over the real archive; 174/174 across sixteen packages. Rendering verified in a browser at desktop and narrow widths in both light and dark themes, with the chip flip and the findings filter exercised by interaction, not assumed.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested. The editor RENDERS and its view-model is verified; no edit has yet been written back through a contract -- that is SCMS-041, which is also what produces the P7 workload. Nothing is deployed.

details.defectFound: editorView accepted an `access` parameter and never consumed it, so a public actor could open a private entry in the editor -- the declaration-without-a-consumer class (NR-scms-004) for the third time, here as an access leak. Caught by its own vector before landing. Fixed; the refusal is notFound rather than forbidden so it does not confirm the subject exists.
details.vectorWeakness: Two early vectors asserted nothing: the first public entry in the corpus is already promoted, so 'publishing is refused without qualification' was passing on an entry that could not be published at all. Corrected to select a public unpublished entry. Same pattern as the SCMS-031 vector that passed for the wrong reason.
details.previewScope: Published as a private artifact carrying the 73 PUBLIC entries only -- no private draft, not even a title. Pure ASCII by construction so a missing charset header cannot mangle it; the first render mojibaked every em-dash before that fix.

claim: Addendum to scms-evidence-040. The preview's data builder seeded a journal by direct append, and the Canon write-boundary gate refused it in CI. The gate was right: content entering Canon must cross a registered contract (DESIGN.md 5), and 'it is only for a preview' is not an exception to that -- it is simply not production. Resolved by moving the file to impl/editor/test/build-preview-fixture.ts, where its actual status as a fixture builder is visible under the gate's existing stated exemption, rather than by carving a new exemption to fit it. Weakening a gate to stop it complaining is how a gate becomes decoration. This also names SCMS-041 precisely: importing a corpus for real has to go through the governed path.

details.note: This record supersedes nothing in scms-evidence-040's substance; it adds a finding discovered after that record was written. Recorded as a new entry because records are append-only and a correction is a new superseding record, never an edit -- a rule this session broke once by rewriting the file in place, which the append-only gate caught immediately.

claim: Creation is a governed operation for the first time, and the real corpus now enters Canon through it. content.create@1 lands a record with a receipt and an emission, refuses creating over an existing subject with recovery that points at the record rather than replacing it, requires owner authority like every other write, and fixes the new record's state to draft/unqualified/unpublished regardless of what the input asks for. The governed importer routes all 215 mapped envelopes through the registry: 215 landed, 0 refused, 215 events emitted, zero direct appends. Re-running it lands nothing twice -- 215 conflicts, no replacement, and zero events, so nobody is told about a change that did not happen. An import without proven authority lands nothing at all. 16/16 migrate vectors, 22/22 contracts vectors.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested. The corpus enters through contracts; no concurrent-editing workload has run yet (SCMS-042), nothing is deployed, and no live state was touched.

details.architecturalGapFound: There was NO create contract. content.revise requires an existing revision, and promote/unpublish act on existing records, so the only way content had ever entered Canon was a direct journal.append -- which DESIGN.md 5 forbids outside canon/contracts/qualification. Every migration and vector did it from a test file, where the write-boundary gate exempts fixture construction by an explicit rule. That exemption, correctly written to allow fixtures, was silently the only thing holding the entire import path up. The gate had pointed at this an hour earlier by refusing the editor preview's data builder; that refusal read as a nuisance about a build script and was in fact the finding.
details.ownerDecisionSurfaced: 51 entries that were 'published' on the old site do NOT arrive published, because content.create@1 will not let a caller supply publication or evidence state. Publishing is qualification plus promotion and neither is inherited by copying. This is either exactly right or an unacceptable amount of ceremony for content that has been live for years -- an owner judgement, so the strict behaviour is implemented and the choice is registered as SH-15 rather than settled quietly.

claim: The editor writes through the contract path and real editing is observable. landEdit() lands an edit via content.revise@1, appending a revision and emitting; a stale edit conflicts, writes nothing, and is recorded with its lane and overlap. Lane assignment follows DESIGN.md 8.5 -- prose is free, titles and tags are bounded, identity and access are required, and a mixed edit takes the strictest lane it touches. Overlap is computed against Canon BEFORE the write, because afterwards it is unrecoverable: a conflict says the revision moved, not whether it moved on the fields this session touched, and that difference is the whole of what P7 turns on. summarizeP7 counts only free-lane overlapping edits and refuses to offer a reading below a stated floor of 30, saying why. 17/17 editor vectors, 26/26 contracts vectors, 188 across sixteen packages.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested for the MECHANISM. P7 is NOT decided and no workload has run. The instrument exists; the evidence does not yet.
details.deliberateNonAction: No synthetic editing workload was generated. DESIGN.md 8.5 deferred P7 pending 'a real editing workload rather than a fixture', and manufacturing edits to produce a recommendation would answer the question with invented data dressed as evidence -- a worse version of this project's recurring failure, because it would look like diligence.
details.defectFound: NR-scms-008: content.revise silently deleted sibling slots via a shallow top-level merge. Editing a body destroyed the title and summary while reporting 'completed'. Found by the overlap detector reporting an overlap that should not have existed -- it was right, about something worse than it was looking for.

claim: No gate in the system reads its deciding input from the caller. Evidence lands via qualification.record-evidence@1 and attestations via qualification.attest@1, which reads evidence from Canon and never from input; content.promote@1 reads the attestation from Canon and never from input. Vectors confirm a caller cannot hand in a QUALIFIED disposition (the field is not read at all), cannot hand in the evidence deciding its own attestation (with no evidence in Canon the disposition is BLOCKED whatever the request offered), cannot record evidence without declaring when it was observed and when it expires, and cannot attest without owner authority. Re-attesting supersedes the prior verdict, leaving exactly one current answer and both in history with the chain intact. 24/24 qualification vectors, 13/13 e2e, 199 across sixteen packages.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested. Closes forgery of gate inputs. Does NOT close self-attestation -- an owner can still record evidence for their own work, which is SH-13 and is policy, not repair.
details.testRun: node --test across 16 packages, 199 pass / 0 fail, node v25.4.0, 2026-08-29
details.thirdInstance: This is the third recorded instance of one failure: the party being gated supplying the value that decides the gate -- promotionAuthority (NR-scms-005), the consequence profile (NR-scms-006), and the attestation itself. Moving attestations into Canon WITHOUT moving evidence would have relocated the hole rather than closing it, since qualify() takes evidence as an argument.
details.strengthening: An attestation can no longer be borrowed from another revision. It used to arrive in the request, so a mismatch had to be DETECTED and yielded 'conflict'; it is now looked up by the requested revision, so presenting the wrong one is not expressible. The check became unnecessary rather than merely reliable.
details.modellingForced: (1) Evidence must carry observedAt and expiresAt. Classifying it as 'declared' to dodge rr-rsp's freshness rule would have meant choosing a provenance class to avoid saying how long evidence is good for, which makes EQP's STALE validity uncomputable. (2) Re-attestation must supersede: the first version appended a second current record under the same subject, so the lookup returned the withdrawn verdict. Caught by the composed spine.

claim: R2 has delivery. A new subscriber receives a backfill burst of everything it may see, live delivery follows, and replay from EVERY cursor position -- the null backfill cursor and every mid-stream reconnect point -- loses nothing the subscriber may see, which is P10's stated no-event-loss criterion. A subscriber beyond the burst limit receives an explicit lagged disclosure naming catch-up-then-live, and catchUp() executes that recovery to a terminating non-lagged phase. Lag is measured in the subscriber's own relevant stream, not the global one: a vector makes 100 changes to a subject the subscriber cannot see and asserts the delivery is NOT lagged, because reporting the global figure would turn the lag message into a side channel for write volume. A lens narrows only -- a lens naming a subject outside the accessible dependency set grants nothing. Silence stays silence: a caught-up subscriber and a subscriber whose invisible neighbour changed both receive no message rather than an empty one. The wire carries invalidation keys and never content. 10/10 vectors; 209 across seventeen packages.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested for transport SEMANTICS, in memory, in one process. NOT established: network, durability, real latency, reconnection over a dropped socket, ordering under concurrency, or any measurement against 8.6 degradation budgets -- which do not exist yet (SH-6).

details.propertyAtRisk: Lag measured on the global pending stream would disclose global write volume to any subscriber -- the same inference SCMS-026 closed by sending silence rather than empty notifications, reintroduced while looking like a helpful protocol message. Relevance is therefore computed before burst limiting.
details.reuse: Who-is-told remains SCMS-026's fanOut, called with the subjects in the delivery window, so there is one implementation of the non-leak rule rather than two.

claim: The editor runs and saves. A zero-dependency Node server imports all 215 entries through content.create@1 at startup, loads prose from the owner's checkout at runtime without vendoring it, and lands every save through content.revise@1 -- verified by interaction: an edit was made in a browser, the chip flipped to 'local, unsent', saving reported a revision appended with the outbox at 216 events, and the P7 observation was written with lane 'bounded' (a title is not prose, so it correctly does not count toward P7). The server registers every implemented contract rather than the narrow path, and reads `qualified` from Canon via the attestation exactly as the promotion gate does, so the UI refuses Publish for the same reason the contract does rather than offering a second opinion.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + VERIFIED BY INTERACTION, which is a lower rung than the rest of this system. The server is thin glue over individually-vectored modules and has no vectors of its own; it borrows none of their coverage.
details.persistence: Edits append to a JSONL outside the repository and replay through the contract path on restart. This is development-grade custody so a night's work survives a restart, and explicitly NOT the durability decision -- SH-1 remains open.
details.ownerCorrection: The owner pointed out that a published artifact is not a usable editor. They were right: P7 is to be settled by real edits and a page that cannot save produces none. What had been delivered was the appearance of the instrument.
details.corpusObservation: The Medium-imported articles carry a stray '---' horizontal rule immediately after the frontmatter, so it renders as the body's first line. That is owner content, not a parser defect, and has been left alone -- silently stripping characters from ~140 articles is an edit, and edits are the owner's to make. It is visible in the editor, which is where it can be decided about.

claim: The editor is a surface. It resolves a ResolvedSurface with purpose 'edit' via the request impl/authoring already declared, reads membership from it, and hydrates content only for surface members -- the same look-up-never-look-around discipline deriveFeed holds. The index likewise resolves a collection surface instead of scanning the journal. Both hand-rolled access comparisons are gone, so the read path now has exactly ONE implementation of the access rule. Operation exposure comes from the resolved surface; domain preconditions (already published, no attestation, conflicted) stay in the view-model, which is the SSS-INV-010 line between exposure and permission. SH-16's own falsifiable test passes: the authoring surface expresses two materially different ways with identical presented order and identical exposed operations, while morphology differs -- so the surface is not underspecified and the hand-written page was not carrying meaning the model lacks. 20/20 editor vectors; 210/210 across seventeen packages; the running server verified unchanged by smoke test.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested. Establishes that the authoring surface is expressible twice; establishes nothing about a voice adapter being USABLE for authoring, which is a human-factors question no vector settles.

details.whatThisRemoved: Two duplicate access comparisons -- one in editorView, one in editorIndex. A second implementation of an access rule is a second chance to get it wrong, which is exactly how NR-scms-004 (declared flag with no consumer) and NR-scms-006 (a guard that failed open) happened. The access-leak vector from SCMS-040 still passes, and now passes through the resolver rather than through the removed local check.
details.declaredDifference: The editor's collection lens deliberately omits the reader's `listed === true` predicate: an author must see unlisted and unpublished work, a reader must not. Same resolver, different lens, and a vector asserts the difference in both directions so it stays declared rather than emergent.
